Q: SAF listFiles() returns empty for subfolders even when using buildDocumentUriUsingTree A:

This happens because document URIs are being mixed with tree URIs.

On Android 11+, SAF permissions apply only to the tree URI that the user originally selected. When a document URI (even one obtained from DocumentFile.listFiles()) is reconstructed or rebound manually, it loses its association with the granted tree permission. When this happens, DocumentFile.listFiles() silently returns an empty array.

DocumentsContract.buildDocumentUriUsingTree() does not restore permission context if the URI was already detached from the original tree.

What not to do

  • Do not rebuild child URIs manually
  • Do not mix fromSingleUri() and fromTreeUri()
  • Do not pass document URIs back into SAF expecting them to retain tree permissions

Correct approach

Keep the DocumentFile hierarchy intact and recurse using DocumentFile objects, not URIs.

    void scan(DocumentFile dir) {
        for (DocumentFile child : dir.listFiles()) {
            if (child.isDirectory()) {
                scan(child);
            } else {
                // handle file
            }
        }
    }

Entry point (only once)

    DocumentFile root =
            DocumentFile.fromTreeUri(context, treeUri);

    scan(root);

Key rule

Never reconstruct or re-parse child URIs when using SAF. Only recurse using the DocumentFile instances returned by listFiles().

Why this works

  • SAF grants permission to a tree, not arbitrary document URIs.
  • DocumentFile preserves the permission context internally.
  • Rebuilding URIs breaks the tree association, causing empty results.

Q: After upgrade, Flyway initialization fails with "Unknown prefix for location" A:

Issue resolved by switching the order of the Gradle dependencies:

implementation(libs.flyway.postgresql)
implementation(libs.flyway.core)

And creating src/main/resources/META-INF/services/org.flywaydb.core.extensibility.Plugin with the list of plugin classes to register.

The root cause - that ShadowJar's task mergeServiceFiles() isn't properly merging Java Service Provider Interface (SPI) files from multiple Flyway jars. Flyway uses Java's ServiceLoader to discover location handlers via META-INF/services/org.flywaydb.core.extensibility.Plugin, and in my case, because my PostgreSQL plugin was listed after Flyway core, it overwritten the plugins available by Flyway core - including the plugin for fetching a classloader resource. The giveaway was the empty list of available plugins in the error message - the part where it said should be one of had an empty list. The reason I saw the callback path is that this is an automatic step during initialization that's generally fails silently if it's not there.

Q: Why subsetting a complex survey design with replicate weights is slow? A:

I think it's as.svrepdesign() rather than subset() being slow here. If you don't rely on Jacknife, you could try bootstrap, which is much faster; increase replicates= (defaults to 50) to somewhat higher, say 1,000 or more.

> library(tictoc)
> # Creation of replicate weights using jacknife
> tic()
> eusilc_design_rep <- 
+   as.svrepdesign(eusilc_design, type="JKn")
> toc()
193.857 sec elapsed
> # Creation of replicate weights using bootstrap
> tic()
> eusilc_design_rep <- 
+   as.svrepdesign(eusilc_design, type="bootstrap",
+   replicates=1e3,   
+   mse=TRUE)
> toc()
9.366 sec elapsed
> # Subsetting
> tic()
> subset_test_survey <- subset(eusilc_design_rep , eqIncome < 1500)
> toc()  ## actually negligible
0.005 sec elapsed
